diagnosis.causal_judgment: silence-detector's core model — 'initial segment is low-energy, content begins when smoothed energy exceeds baseline × multiplier' — contradicts the task's documented reality that the opening is noisy static. Because the baseline window (first 60s) sat entirely inside the noisy opening, the threshold was inflated and the detector mislabeled 0–221s as 'silence,' deleting ~140s of actual teaching content. The skill offered no validation, no fallback (e.g., detect energy drop into content, or cross-check with video-frame variance), and no guidance on when its assumption is invalid, so the agent propagated the bad boundary into pause detection and final cutting. Over-specific default parameters and under-specified unit/boundary contracts with pause-detector and segment-combiner compound the failure, matching the repair-hint locations.
rewrite_targets: Reframe silence-detector around the actual phenomenon: detect the opening as a prefix whose characteristic differs from teaching speech (e.g., energy drop into content, or variance/spectral change), not simply 'low energy then high energy'.

Add explicit input-validation and sanity checks: reject or flag opening lengths beyond a plausibility bound (e.g., >20% of total duration) and require a secondary signal (frame-difference, spectral flatness) before accepting.

Document the time-unit and boundary contract (seconds, inclusive start / exclusive end) and how smoothing-window interacts with per-second energy indices; mirror this in video-processor and segment-combiner call notes.
Replace hard-coded defaults (1.5 / 60 / 30) with discovery rules or adaptive estimation tied to observed energy distribution; keep literals only if proven task-family invariant.
Add a fallback path: if detector output is implausible, fall back to frame-based static-opening detection or to a conservative short opening cut.

Clarify pause-detector threshold_ratio semantics (relative to local window mean? median?) and align the description across silence-detector and video-processor so parameters mean the same thing end-to-end.
Trim background prose to stay under the 220-word prior and tighten to an explicit workflow with checkpoints.
diagnosis.summary: The skill's opening-detection abstraction (low-energy prefix → transition to high energy) contradicts the task's noisy-static opening, so it reported a 221s opening and removed ~140s of teaching content. Combined with no plausibility check, no fallback, and under-specified inter-skill unit/parameter contracts, the pipeline produced a mathematically consistent but semantically wrong compression. Fix by re-grounding the detector in the real signal, adding validation/fallbacks, and tightening parameter and boundary contracts across silence-detector, pause-detector, segment-combiner, and video-processor.
